### LOW: Opt\-in resident\-RAM prefix\-cache bank contradicts T\-041's "no production RAM tier" posture
[changelog\.d/nemotron\-super\-media\-discovery\.md:57](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/7c548f8d33969be2674569852f8797eaed72b137/changelog.d/nemotron-super-media-discovery.md#L57) · T-028, T-041

The changelog adds \`DARKBLOOM\_PREFIX\_CACHE\_MEMORY=1\`, which opts the Nemotron Super owner into a resident recurrent checkpoint bank for exact text prefix reuse\. The bank is sized from the KV grant and its budget is reserved from load until retirement\. T\-041 and its mitigations state that production never constructs or funds a resident\-RAM prefix cache, and that the only tier is the encrypted SSD tier with coordinator\-authored account/model cacheSalt scoping\. The changelog says client prompt\-cache keys are rejected\. It does not say whether the bank is keyed by the coordinator's authenticated cacheSalt, so cross\-account reuse and TTFT timing leakage through this tier cannot be ruled out from the supplied text\. The bank also has no stated TTL, KEK protection or purge: checkpoints are plaintext recurrent state in process RAM\. This is the SEC\-035 oracle class, and also affects T\-028/T\-011 residue in process memory\. The path is opt\-in and its builder is described as unregistered, so this is a threat\-model gap rather than a confirmed regression\. Fix: before the hook is registered, extend T\-041 with this tier's scoping, lifetime, wipe\-on\-retirement and timing posture, and require the coordinator cacheSalt in the bank key\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: Threat model does not cover new Nemotron Super local prefix\-cache bank \(resident RAM tier, local unscoped cache scope\)
[docs/architecture/inference\.md:128](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/7c548f8d33969be2674569852f8797eaed72b137/docs/architecture/inference.md#L128) · A-001, T-041

The new documentation describes \`NemotronSuperLocalPrefixCache\`, which gives the plain owner a resident recurrent checkpoint bank when \`DARKBLOOM\_PREFIX\_CACHE\_MEMORY=1\`, and says text requests use 'the local unscoped cache scope'\. T\-041 states that production never constructs or funds a resident\-RAM prefix cache, and that the single \`DARKBLOOM\_PREFIX\_CACHE\` gate controls an encrypted SSD tier whose scope is coordinator\-authored per account\. The new bank is a separate env gate, resident in RAM, unencrypted, and not scoped by account\. The doc says the paths are unregistered and not exposed over HTTP, and that no production caller installs the hook, so this is not an active regression\. If the owner is later wired to production, it would reintroduce a cross\-tenant sharing and TTFT oracle that T\-041 and SEC\-035 treat as closed or narrowed\. T\-041 should be updated to say this bank is out of production scope, or to cover it, before any wiring\. Add a note requiring cacheScope plumbing and a fresh SEC\-035 sign\-off\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

findings.detail: The changelog says `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1` opts the Nemotron Super owner into exact text prefix reuse. It uses a resident recurrent checkpoint bank, sized from the KV grant (`min(1 GiB, grant/8)`), and reserved from load until retirement. T-041 and its mitigations say production never constructs or funds a resident-RAM prefix cache, that DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE is the single gate, and that the only tier is encrypted SSD with HMAC names, a 30-minute TTL and a KEK purge. A RAM bank is a second reuse path. It has no stated tie to the cacheSalt/account scoping, a different TTL, a different purge path, and a hit/miss TTFT oracle (SEC-035) that lives only in process memory and is not covered by at-rest encryption. Trigger: an operator sets the variable and the provider serves multi-account traffic. Impact: cross-tenant prefix-presence inference if reuse is not keyed by the coordinator-authored cacheSalt. I could not verify the source, so this is a documentation/threat-model gap and not a confirmed code flaw. Fix: update T-041 and TB-007 to cover this opt-in tier. State that it is default-off, that entries are keyed by cacheSalt, what the lifetime and purge are, and that it is cleared on unload. Confirm in source that the salt is part of the lookup key.
findings.title: Opt-in resident RAM prefix-cache bank contradicts T-041's 'no production RAM tier' assumption
